## Knowledge Submission
- From: medici
- Type: pattern
- Scope: team-wide
- Urgency: standard
- Related: stage-2-confirms-filing-gate.md (knowledge-health adjacency); none direct
- Confidence: high

### Content
**Provenance-coverage % per corpus segment is a trackable knowledge-health metric.** Measure the share of files carrying source/provenance markers, computed PER corpus segment (wiki / topics / docs / scratchpads / etc.), not corpus-wide. Two payoffs:

1. It turns "are we contamination-exposed?" (an inference hardening into stated-fact, undetected) into a dashboard number per segment.
2. It directly predicts where provenance-traversal recovery (apex-research's "Mode B" truth-tree traversal, which follows `source:`/`related:` links from a contamination point to its dependents) has REACH vs. is BLIND. A segment with low provenance coverage has no edges to traverse -- traversal-based recovery is a no-op there regardless of how good the procedure is. Coverage-% is the leading indicator for traversal reach.

The metric is cheap to compute (grep for frontmatter source markers, ratio per directory) and re-runnable each session as a trend line.

### Evidence
Measured baseline of FR's own corpus (2026-06-26, during apex #176 Q3 evaluation):
- wiki: ~99% (322/325 files carry source markers; 232 carry `related:` traversal edges)
- docs: ~half (41/83)
- topics: low (12 large design-doc files, citation-sparse; near-zero internal cross-refs in topics 02/05/08)
- scratchpads: 14/15 carry some ref marker

Origin: apex-research's contamination-recovery methodology (Discussion #176, playbook `teams/apex-research/playbooks/contamination-recovery.md`, battle-test `inventory/dokosign-battle-test-report.md`). This metric is my distillation of the most reusable knowledge-health instrument from that methodology -- the procedure's own implied health signal.
summary: Protocol A: provenance-coverage % as health metric

## Knowledge Submission
- From: medici
- Type: pattern
- Scope: team-wide
- Urgency: standard
- Related: [ORPHAN-CLAIM audit category in prompts/medici.md §Audit Checklist]; the provenance-coverage-% metric I just submitted (sibling lesson, same apex #176 origin)
- Confidence: high

### Content
**Authoring-time prevention vs. audit-time detection are two distinct control points for the same failure mechanic** (a model-knowledge inference hardening into "sourced fact"). They are not interchangeable -- they sit at OPPOSITE points in the lifecycle:

- **Authoring-time prevention:** a rule enforced AT WRITE TIME -- e.g. "every claim must be traceable to a local file or be tagged `[speculative]`." The claim cannot enter the corpus unprovenanced in the first place. (This is apex-research's posture, in their common-prompt.)
- **Audit-time detection:** a PERIODIC sweep that catches unprovenanced claims AFTER they're already in the corpus -- e.g. FR's `[ORPHAN-CLAIM]` audit category. Detection finds contamination that already happened; it does not stop it from being written.

The naming the distinction is the durable lesson: when assessing a corpus's contamination posture, identify WHICH control point a given safeguard occupies. A team can have strong detection and zero prevention (FR's current state) -- same failure mechanic, opposite control point, very different exposure profile.

Concrete FR-specific gap surfaced by this lens: FR's topic/design-doc layer has NO authoring-time provenance rule AND no `related:` edges. That makes it FR's most exposed surface -- inferences can be written as fact unprovenanced (no prevention) and there's no traversal graph for after-the-fact recovery either.

NOTE (per team-lead): file the DISTINCTION as knowledge. Whether FR should ADOPT an authoring-time provenance rule on the topic layer is a separate PO call -- NOT a decision being recorded here. This submission is the conceptual distinction + the measured gap, not a recommendation to act.

### Evidence
Surfaced 2026-06-26 during apex #176 Q3 evaluation. apex's authoring-time rule: `teams/apex-research/playbooks/contamination-recovery.md` §"Connection to the provenance tagging rule" + apex common-prompt "Provenance Tagging -- Local File vs Model Knowledge." FR's audit-time analog: `[ORPHAN-CLAIM]` category, `prompts/medici.md` §Audit Checklist (ratified #74, 2026-06-05; baseline sweep `docs/health-report-competency-gap-2026-06-05.md`). FR's exposed topic layer measured in the sibling provenance-coverage-% submission.
summary: Protocol A: authoring-time prevention vs audit-time detection
